title: Graceful Tuning Safety Layer for Batching & Cache Autoconfig
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a safety-first orchestration layer that applies automated batching and KV-cache recommendations gradually with enforced latency/throughput SLO guardrails. The feature must: 1) provide staged config apply (canary->ramp->full) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions, 2) surface per-route and per-model impact metrics in Console, 3) implement limiters (concurrency and token-rate) as temporary fallbacks, 4) enable SLO-aware routing to shift traffic between variants when optimization attempts risk violating latency/throughput targets, and 5) include anomaly detection tuned for token-latency and tail-percentiles to avoid noisy rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New endpoint /admin/autotune/apply exposes canary/ramp/full modes and returns deterministic plan diffs; 2) Autoscale/limiters will be injected and reversible by the controller within 30s of detection; 3) Console shows live canary metrics (p50, p95, p99 latency, tokens/s, success-rate) with change indicators; 4) Anomaly detector triggers rollback if p99 latency increases >30% and absolute p99 exceeds route SLO for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets; 5) All applied configs must be auditable with user + commit metadata; 6) Feature has e2e tests and a gradual rollout to 10%->50%->100% with manual override.
technical_notes: Design uses controller-operator pattern in inference control-plane. Apply plan composes: (a) batching_profile, (b) kv_cache_policy, (c) limiter_overlay. Canary runs route-level traffic split to plan variant. Monitoring relies on existing ingestion (metrics-mux) and a lightweight anomaly microservice that computes rolling window deltas on tail latencies and token throughput. Rollback is initiated by controller when anomaly service emits a v2 'slo_violation' event. Rate limiters are soft by default (grace period counter) and harden on persistent violation. We'll reuse kernel scheduling hints from runtime and extend audit logs to include plan hashes and GitHub PR URLs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from noisy p99s during load spikes. Mitigation: use hysteresis (3 consecutive buckets) and correlate with tokens/s drop to detect contention vs traffic shift. Risk: canary starving other tenants on shared pools. Mitigation: prefer tenant-aware routing and enforce pool-level quotas; prefer Dedicated pool tests first. Risk: rollback thrash under flapping anomalies. Mitigation: backoff window 10 minutes before reattempt and expose manual pause in Console.
